title: Redwood Optimize v2 — Product Overview, PRD, Design Spec, Roadmap & Pricing (v2.0)
author: Sofia Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose
This document consolidates the product overview, PRD, high-level design, roadmap, pricing/packaging proposal, and release notes for Redwood Optimize v2 (internal name: optimize-v2). Optimize v2 is the next iteration of the Redwood Optimize product: a cost-and-performance toolkit that provides automated batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization recommendations, and workload-aware model selection to reduce per-token inference cost while maintaining output quality.

Audience
- Product, Eng (serving-runtime, infra, platform), Applied ML, Sales, and Customer Success.

Executive summary
- Goal: Reduce average hosted inference cost by 30% vs. baseline (optimize-v1) for typical production workloads while keeping quality regressions <1% on tracked eval sets.
- Target customers: AI-native startups, mid-market product teams, and platform teams using hosted or dedicated deployments.
- Primary differentiators: workload-aware suggestions, automated batching rulesets, and per-route observability tying cost back to prompts and eval sets.

Goals & success metrics
- Cost reduction: mean per-token cost decrease >= 30% (primary KPI).
- Quality retention: no more than 1% degradation on canonical prompt sets per model (tracked via evals).
- Adoption: 25% of active hosted accounts enable Optimize features within 6 months of GA.
- Revenue: convert 10% of Optimize users to paid Dedicated or Optimize add-on within 12 months.

Use cases
- Throughput-first apps: chat assistants and search reranking that need lower unit cost without increased latency.
- Cost-sensitive scale ups: SaaS companies with high embedding/token volumes that want automated cost savings.
- Platform standardization: central platform teams that want consistent configuration and observability across teams.

Non-goals
- Replace full custom quantization tooling (we provide recommendations and supported quantized variants but not a full quantization toolchain).
- Autonomous model training or architecture search.

High-level product requirements (PRD)
1) Functional requirements
1.1 Workload profiling and recommendations
- Provide per-route profiling: token distribution, sequence length histogram, KV-cache hit rate estimate, and batching potential.
- Recommend batching and cache configs (batch size target, max wait time, prefix caching enabled/disabled, cache TTL) with expected cost delta estimates.
- Expose a one-click apply flow for Hosted customers and a config artifact for Dedicated/Private.

1.2 Automatic batching engine (runtime integration)
- Integrate with serving runtime to apply continuous batching policies per model/route.
- Constraints: respect per-request latency SLO (default 120ms p95 for interactive routes).
- Expose observability: batching efficiency, queued requests, average batch size, and latency distribution.

1.3 Caching and prefix/KV reuse
- Track prefix reuse across requests; provide remote KV-cache option for dedicated/private deployments.
- Policies: TTL-based eviction, size-based eviction, and per-route inclusion/exclusion.

1.4 Quantization and model variant recommendations
- Maintain a catalog of verified model variants (FP16, 4-bit quantized variants) with measured perf/quality tradeoffs for common sequence lengths.
- Provide recommendation engine that maps workload to a model variant with estimated cost/latency/quality delta.

1.5 Observability and quality guardrails
- Per-route cost breakdown (tokens, batching, cache hits, model variant selector).
- Alerting for quality regressions: tie model/variant changes to eval sets and trigger regression alerts when metrics fall beyond thresholds.

2) Non-functional requirements
- Security: support KMS integration for private deployments; do not persist PII in analysis payloads by default.
- Performance: additional Optimize logic must not add >3ms median extra overhead to request path when enabled.
- Scalability: profiling and recommendations must support customers with 10k QPS peaks in Dedicated.

3) UX requirements
- Console: per-route Optimize panel with current recommendations, applied configs, expected savings, and preview of potential quality impact.
- API: `POST /v1/optimize/profile` to profile a route, `GET /v1/optimize/recommendations/{route}` to fetch recommendations, `PUT /v1/routes/{route}/optimize` to apply. Provide SDK helpers in JS/Python.

Design specification (high level)

Architecture overview
- Components:
  - Profiler service (offline + online): gathers sample statistics, aggregates histograms, and computes recommenders. Owned by eng-serving-runtime and product.
  - Recommendation engine: runs rules + ML-based selector to produce parameterized suggestions.
  - Runtime batching integration: kernel-level hooks and scheduler changes to support per-route continuous batching.
  - Cache subsystem: in-memory local cache for hosted, remote Redis-like cache for Dedicated/Private.
  - Console + API: UX layer to present recommendations and apply configs.

Data flows
1. Probe traffic sampler (edge) -> Profiler (streamed metrics + sampled payloads)
2. Profiler aggregates histograms (seq len, token distribution, kv reuse) -> Recommendation engine
3. Engine outputs candidate configs (batch size, max latency window, cache TTL, model variant) with estimated cost/quality impacts -> Console & API
4. Customer applies config -> Runtime applies batching/cache/model variant selectors -> Metrics emitted to dashboards + eval comparator for quality.

Implementation notes and constraints
- Profiling sample rate default: 1 in 200 requests for hosted; configurable for dedicated.
- Use approximate histograms (DDSketch/HD Histogram) to bound memory.
- Recommendation model must be deterministic for a given profile snapshot to make rollout auditing simpler.

API contract (examples)
- POST /v1/optimize/profile
  - body: {"route_id": "string", "window_seconds": 3600}
  - response: {"profile_id": "string", "summary": "string"}
- GET /v1/optimize/recommendations/{route_id}
  - response: {"recommendations": [ {"id": "r1", "batch_size": 16, "max_latency_ms": 50, "model_variant": "m-llama2-q4_0", "estimated_savings_pct": 28, "quality_risk_pct": 0.4 } ] }
Note: the above examples are illustrative; final API shapes live in eng-developer-experience/api-examples.

Quality & evals
- Every recommendation that changes model variant must be evaluated against the route's canonical prompt set using the evaluation harness (applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness).
- Regression threshold: if any tracked metric (BLEU/accuracy/semantic-similarity) degrades by >1.0% absolute, block the rollout and surface to Product/Applied ML for triage.

Roadmap & themes (next 12 months)
- Q1 2026 (Discovery + Infra): Profiler MVP, recommendation engine prototype, UI mockups, initial APIs.
- Q2 2026 (Beta): Runtime batching integration, cache subsystem baseline, console workflow, early hosted beta with 10 pilot customers.
- Q3 2026 (GA): Hardened recommendations, expanded model variant catalog, pricing & packaging announced, Dedicated support for remote cache and private catalog.
- Q4 2026 (Optimize for scale): Auto-rollouts, ML-driven policy tuning, multi-tenant cost attribution, and out-of-the-box presets for common workloads.

Milestones and owners
- Profiler service (owner: Eng - serving-runtime, lead: Priya Natarajan) — Q1 Q2 2026
- Runtime batching (owner: Eng - infra and serving-runtime, lead: Marcus Osei) — Q2 2026
- Console UI and APIs (owner: Eng - developer-experience, lead: Jordan Park) — Q2 2026
- Evaluation integration (owner: Applied ML, lead: Marta Alvarez) — Q2 2026
- Pricing & packaging (owner: Product - Sofia Patel) — Q3 2026

Pricing & packaging proposal
- Objective: provide clear ROI and low friction adoption while offering an upsell path to Dedicated/Private.

Proposed SKUs
1) Optimize (Hosted) — free tier + consumption add-on
- Free tier: basic profiling and 3 recommendations per month; limited to 7-day retention of profiling data.
- Pro add-on (metered): $0.002 per profiled 1000 tokens (pricing example) OR $99/month per route for unlimited profiling and recommendations, plus 90-day retention of profiling data.
- Benefit: attractive for SMBs and startups to see savings before committing.

2) Optimize (Dedicated) — enterprise add-on
- Subscription: $2,500/month per Dedicated pool + variable usage credit model (or negotiated enterprise rate). Includes remote cache, private model variant catalog, extended retention, and prioritized recommendations.

3) Professional services & onboarding
- One-time onboarding packages starting at $10k for enterprise customers for custom profiling, SLO tuning, and runbook setup.

Estimated savings modeling (example)
- Sample workload: 60M tokens/month baseline cost $6,000/month. Predicted saving 30% => $1,800/month saved. With Optimize Pro at $99/month, ROI in first month. For dedicated customers, cost calculus uses committed GPU costs; Optimize can justify larger contracts by reducing consumed GPU hours.

Packaging notes
- Enablement is opt-in per route; defaults are safe and reversible.
- Trial: 30-day Optimize Pro trial for hosted customers who cross 5M tokens/month.
- Billing: integrate with existing usage billing. For metered pricing, report: profiled_tokens, recommendations_applied, estimated_savings.

Rollout & release plan (GA)
1) Beta (select customers)
- Target: 10 pilot customers across SMB and mid-market.
- Duration: 8 weeks.
- Objectives: verify savings, measure quality delta, validate console flows.
- Acceptance: average savings >=20% for pilot cohort and no blocked regressions.

2) GA
- Canary rollout to 5% of accounts with traffic > 1k QPS equivalent, gradually increase over 4 weeks.
- Guardrails: require daily regression checks and auto-rollback policy if quality regression >1% on canonical sets or latency SLOs exceed 10% above baseline.

3) Post-GA
- Expand model variant catalog, add ML-tuned recommender, and promote Dedicated packaging.

Operational runbook excerpt
- Monitor: optimize/metrics/batching_efficiency, optimize/metrics/cache_hit_rate, optimize/quality/regression_alerts.
- On regression alert:
  1. Pager to Applied ML + Product on-call.
  2. Re-run evals with recent traffic snapshot.
  3. If regression confirmed, rollback applied Optimize config and create triage ticket.

Release notes — v2.0 (2026-03-15)
- GA features included:
  - Workload profiler (route-level histograms and KV reuse estimates).
  - Recommendation engine alpha (rules-based + deterministic heuristics).
  - Runtime continuous-batching integration for hosted models (per-route batch size and latency window controls).
  - Console Optimize panel with one-click apply and preview of estimated savings.
  - Basic quantized model catalog integration (m-llama2-q4_0, m-flan-t5-q4_0).

Known limitations
- Initial recommendation engine does not yet include ML-driven personalization; it's rules-based and conservative by design.
- Remote cache for Dedicated is alpha and requires customer provisioning of cache storage.

Open risks and mitigations
- Quality regressions: enforced eval gating and conservative defaults; applied configs cannot change model_variant without passing eval checks.
- Runtime overhead: performance budget defined; profiling disabled by default and sampling rate tunable.

Appendices
A. Example configuration snippet (Console -> API application)\nPUT /v1/routes/chat-assistant-1/optimize
Body (example):
{
  "enabled": true,
  "batching": {"target_batch_size": 16, "max_wait_ms": 50},
  "cache": {"enabled": true, "ttl_seconds": 300},
  "model_variant": "m-llama2-q4_0",
  "apply_mode": "canary",
  "canary_pct": 5
}

B. Contacts & ownership
- Product lead: Sofia Patel (product) — owner of pricing and roadmap questions.
- Engineering leads: Priya Natarajan (eng-serving-runtime), Marcus Osei (eng-infra), Jordan Park (eng-developer-experience).
- Applied ML: Marta Alvarez — evals and regression triage.

D. Approval checklist (pre-GA)
- [ ] Pilot cohort results validated and documented
- [ ] Evals: no regression >1% on canonical prompt sets
- [ ] Console flows QA'ed on Chrome/Firefox and mobile view
- [ ] Pricing approved by Finance & GTM

For questions or to request early access for a customer, contact the product lead or file a ticket in #product-optimize.
